segments.t: SSH tunnels securely forward traffic between local and remote ports through an encrypted SSH connection. korTTY supports three tunnel types: local port forwarding, remote port forwarding, and dynamic port forwarding (SOCKS proxy).
Open a connection for editing: KTPH000Connections KTPH004 Manage ConnectionsKTPH001 → select the connection → KTPH002EditKTPH003.
Navigate to the KTPH000SSH TunnelsKTPH001 tab.
Click KTPH000Add TunnelKTPH001 and configure the tunnel.
Target host from the SSH server's perspective
Target port on the remote host
Toggle on/off without deleting the configuration
Multiple tunnels can be configured per connection. Disabled tunnels remain in the configuration but are not activated when the connection opens.
Forward a local port to a remote service through the SSH tunnel.
KTPH000Example use case:KTPH001 Access a remote database server that is not directly reachable from your machine.
Once configured, connect to the remote database using KTPH000 on your machine.
Make a local service accessible from the remote server's network.
KTPH000Example use case:KTPH001 Allow a remote team member to access a local development server on your machine.
KTPH001Remote Port:KTPH002 KTPH000 (the port the remote side uses to reach your service)
After connecting, the remote machine can access your service at KTPH000.
Create a SOCKS5 proxy for all network traffic through the SSH tunnel.
KTPH000Example use case:KTPH001 Encrypt all traffic from your browser or application by routing it through the SSH tunnel.
KTPH001Local Port:KTPH002 KTPH000 (or any available port)
Configure your browser or application to use KTPH000 as a SOCKS5 proxy. All traffic will be securely forwarded through the SSH server.
For Dynamic Port Forwarding, only the local port is required. The remote host and remote port fields are not used.
KTPH000Enable/Disable:KTPH001 Toggle the KTPH002EnabledKTPH003 checkbox on a tunnel to activate or deactivate it without removing the configuration.
KTPH000Edit:KTPH001 Select a tunnel and modify its settings.
KTPH000Delete:KTPH001 Remove a tunnel from the connection.
KTPH000Multiple Tunnels:KTPH001 Any number of tunnels can be configured on a single connection and activated simultaneously.
Tunnels are established when the SSH connection is opened and remain active for the duration of the session.
When using local or remote port forwarding on ports below 1024 (such as port 80 or 443), your system may require elevated privileges. Use ports 1024 and above to avoid permission issues.
